newsitem.title: UK: Cuba features again on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Cuba features again on sugar freight market.

text.p: Cuba once again took the limelight of London's sugar freight business with Egypt and Syria cited as end-destinations, shipbrokers said on Friday.
Lorico dominated the day's business, fixing two earlier orders and also quoting for new business -- all for bulk sugar from Cuba.
Shipbrokers said Lorico fixed 14,000 tonnes to Syria for 1/14 May and a further 13,000 tonnes to Egypt for April 20/25. Details of the rates were not yet available.
E D & F Man quoted for 3,500 tonnes of bagged sugar from Motril to Syria for the end of April.
Man was also said to have fixed 20/25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic for early May shipment dates.
Elsewhere, South Africa issued a private tender to sell four cargoes of raw sugar for May/June shipment.
Traders said one major European house was thought to have bought at least one of the c & f cargoes on offer for onward shipment to Canada.
South Korea is in the market to buy 14,000 tonnes of raw sugar for May/June and Iran bought three -- and posisibly four -- cargoes of white sugar for shipment between May and July.
